basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 8-9.' and it opens 'VERS. 8-9.-- Habeo duas filias quae necdum cognoverunt virum; educam eas ad vos, et'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 8-9.-- Habeo duas filias quae necdum cognoverunt virum; educam eas ad vos, et abutimini eis, et caetera. Quomodo Lot justus dicatur, si filias suas ad tam nefas scelus tradere voluit, nisi quia scelestius ad comparationem judicavit peccatum quod agitur contra naturam quam quod admittitur naturaliter?
